judgments.reasoning_cat1: The letter itself concedes the terms 'Grandfather' and 'Grandmother' 'have not always been interpreted and applied consistently', and the fix ('or of his or her spouse at the time the grandparent dies') is itself capable of more than one reading as to step- and in-law relationships.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It purports to state one party's interpretation of Section 3-P of the preserved 1981-84 agreement (c018) rather than to amend it, so its status as an operative term is arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear, single-purpose non-retroactivity limitation tied to a fixed date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c031, which it qualifies, and with the general effective-date rule in c020.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The quoted replacement first sentence is garbled and incomplete and the deleted fifth sentence is cut off mid-clause, so the amended text cannot be reconstructed from the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deleting the liquidation-on-expiration sentence while c001 fixes a March 30, 1993 expiry leaves the fate of accumulated leave at term-end unaddressed anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Certain neutrals', 'subject to their availability and Willingness to serve' and 'effectuate the designation process' are all indefinite, and the clause promises only a meeting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 13 (c017) describes this appendix as a letter of understanding 'regarding the designations of Status Quo and Merits Arbitrators', which promises more content than the letter delivers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to 'negotiate the conditions' triggered by an undefined threshold ('when the normal daily order reaches 2500 copies') is an agreement to agree with a vague trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the negotiate-later structures in c036 and c037 and does not conflict with any operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Satisfactory arrangements', the deadline pegged to 'the date the revised Glen Burnie agreement has been put into effect', and 'shall not involve The Times in increased costs' each leave real room for competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with c037, which covers 'additional portions' of the same Lancaster-printed Magazine on the same no-increased-cost condition, but the two are sequenced rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Performance is conditioned on the Times and Union having 'resolved satisfactorily any grievances, differences and disputes' and on the plant 'running', and the obligation is only to negotiate — all indefinite conditions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against c036's Monday-run commitment and against the Edison start-up and arbitration commitments in c005, raising a sequencing question but no clean conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Changing '6-1/2%' to '7.678%' 'to reflect the present welfare contribution percentage' states a rate without stating the base to which it applies, and the recital of what it 'reflects' may not match the operative number.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The base is supplied, if at all, by c002 ('contributions shall be made on this amount') and is expressly limited by c055's no-contribution-on-Earnings-Bonus carve-out and c009 — the core of a welfare-fund contribution dispute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The instruction has an unclosed quotation mark so the exact words to be inserted cannot be identified, and inserting an employee 'after tax deduction from wages of $3.67' into an employer contribution sentence confuses who pays what.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the $3.67 five-shift deduction in c002 without repeating the five-shift cap, and interacts with the 7.678% rate in c038 — a genuine internal mismatch about the contribution amount.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 3/31/87 figure is rendered '§.00' so the first-year casual contribution is unreadable, and 'additional contributions' presupposes a base amount not stated here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with c038's percentage and c002's per-shift deduction to know what casual contributions total; the word 'additional' points to the unproduced Section 13-H.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise textual insertion identified by the words it follows and the sentence it occupies; little to construe on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its meaning depends on the added paragraph in c042, which carves out cases where the Times itself lacked sixty days' notice — a qualification, not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A New York Times part or section regularly inserted in the Sunday or daily newspaper', 'can demonstrate that it did not have sixty (60) days' notice itself' and 'the promptest practicable notice' are each open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It substantially guts the sixty-day requirement just inserted by c041 while disclaiming any modification of 'any other notice requirements pursuant to the Contract', creating a real reconciliation question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A uniform portion of each employee's wage increase' is undefined as to size and as to which increases ('to become effective then or thereafter'), and the diversion right is unilateral in the Union.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Diverting wage increases interacts with the pension and welfare contributions made 'on this amount' under c002 and with the wage-scale schedule in c003, and with the no-increased-cost limit in c044.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Nominal administrative costs', 'fully cooperate' and 'any such alternatives' are all vague standards with no measurable boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies c043's diversion right and echoes the 'no increased costs' conditions in c036-c037, so it fits the instrument's pattern.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple commitment to form a study committee of stated size; no operative entitlement to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses terminally ill employees, so there is nothing to conflict with.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is materially incomplete — 'it will guarantee all Saturday night Bulldog uding routes and relays)' omits the object of the guarantee and the opening parenthesis, so the promise cannot be read.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument defines the Bulldog guarantee, though c028 excepts 'bulldog' routes from the returns procedure, which is a different subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary' is a floating override, and the exception for retroactive 1987 wages paid in 1988 is an intricate carve-out invited to be argued about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats and depends on the same 1988 exclusion built into the 'gross wages' definition in c050, and on the retroactive payments promised by c002, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single fixed percentage applied to a defined term over stated years.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Gross wages' is defined in c050 and adjusted by c051; the pieces fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A stub-period version of c048 with the same fixed rate and a defined period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with c053's payment deadline for that same stub period and with the contract end date in c001.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tying 'gross wages' to a W-2 line item plus two nested exclusions is workable but the phrase 'for the applicable bonus period' against a calendar-year W-2 leaves an edge case for the 1993 stub period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is immediately qualified by c051, which adds non-W-2 disability and workers' compensation amounts, and by c055's exclusion of the bonus from fund contributions; those fit together but must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To the extent that such State disability and workers' compensation benefits do not appear on the employee's W-2 Form' is a workable but fact-dependent qualifier tied to 'those shifts for which an employee receives benefits'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands the W-2-based definition in c050 and interacts with c055's rule that the Times reports wage rates as increased by $25.93 for disability and compensation purposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single unambiguous payment deadline referenced to 'the applicable bonus period'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the different deadlines in c053 (thirty days after March 30, 1993) and c054 (sixty days after termination), which could be read as competing timetables for the same final bonus.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Allocated in the manner set forth in Paragraph 7' is an imprecise cross-reference, and 'the continuation or other disposition' plus the $25.93 fallback at 'the Union's option' leaves the mechanics arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paragraph 7 (c054) is a termination right rather than an allocation formula, and its sixty-day payout rule sits against this clause's thirty-day rule for the same stub bonus.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause contains a plain date error ('March 39, 1993') and the phrase 'any fringe benefit ... negotiated by any other union and the Times in connection with the current extension negotiations Or at any time through March' is grammatically tangled and open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the paragraph cross-referenced by c053 but does not supply the allocation method that clause assumes, and it overlaps with the most-favoured-nation right in c006 to adopt other unions' benefits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph first requires every wage-rate-based benefit, 'including by example, but not limitation, Times retirement or pension benefits', to be computed as if scales were $25.93 higher, then carves out Welfare and Pension Fund contributions — a general-versus-specific tension sharpened by the vague anti-duplication sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts directly against the contribution obligations in c002 ('Pension and welfare contributions shall be made on this amount'), c038's 7.678% and c009, which is precisely the welfare-fund contribution question this record presents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The number in the first sentence of Paragraph 3 is now eighty-eight (88)' identifies neither what the number counts nor the sentence's text, so the amendment is unintelligible standing alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The referenced Paragraph 3 sits in the 1981-84 booklet memorandum preserved by c018 and as changed by a 1984 memorandum, so the operative text must be assembled from documents outside this instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deleting 'the sentence providing for certain floormen being available for driving assignments' identifies the target only by description, and 'certain floormen' is itself indefinite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the floor-situation and chauffeur creations in c021-c022 and with the external Paragraph 3 amended by c056, leaving the resulting text uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The memorandum is descriptive rather than promissory, and the list of three drop locations is garbled with one entry missing its street, so the 'present practice' it fixes cannot be fully read.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the content given to the 'present Practices' side letter (c029), which extends to the Times' whole direct operation while this memo covers only the West Side Direct area — a scope mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Putting 'abolition' in quotation marks and preserving 'any other agreement contained therein or otherwise regarding those routes other than that portion Providing for attrition' is a partial-survival formula whose reach is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies Appendix B's flat statement in c026 that the November 22, 1983 memorandum 'shall be abolished', and the priority rule in c018 would then have to decide which text governs.
